name: Simple Note

angles.text: For young tauren beginning in Red Cloud Mesa, the note shows that protecting the tribe matters as much as spiritual callings such as shamanism and druidism.
Harutt Thunderhorn teaches novice tauren warriors to temper their pride and defend Camp Narache from centaur.

faq.answer: Harutt Thunderhorn wrote the summons and sent it through a messenger to young tauren ready for martial training.
Harutt Thunderhorn is a tauren warrior trainer at Camp Narache in Mulgore. He trains new warriors in battle and the ancestral ways of tribal warfare.
The note calls newly awakened warriors to meet their trainer. It reminds them that defenders and hunters are as vital to the tribe as druids and shamans.
faq.q: What is the purpose of the Simple Note?

faq.answer: Hostile centaur packs threaten Mulgore's borders. Harutt trains warriors to hunt them and protect the camp.
faq.q: Why are warriors called upon to hunt centaur?

faq.answer: Camp Narache lies at the edge of Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. It is the ancestral training camp and starting settlement of the young tauren of the Hawkwind tribe.
The text does not name the rites. It says every tribal member, from warriors and hunters to shamans and druids, must undergo them to prove strength, humility, and dedication to their people.
faq.q: What are the tribal rites Harutt mentions?

sections.body: At Camp Narache, a messenger brings young warriors a summons from Harutt Thunderhorn. The veteran trainer calls each fighter to report and begin training to defend the tribe.
sections.title: A Summons to Battle

sections.body: The Shu'halo revere their spiritual leaders, yet Harutt teaches that warriors bear an equal burden. They patrol tribal borders and hunt predatory centaur packs to protect their peaceful kin from attack. Battle may bring glory, but warriors remain humble and complete the same traditional rites as shamans and druids.
sections.title: The Defender's Burden

summary: At Camp Narache, Harutt Thunderhorn calls young tauren warriors to defend their people. His summons reminds them that warriors stand beside druids and shamans in guarding the tribal borders from centaur.
